back: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries (catchment).
The boundary of a drainage basin, usually a line of high ground.
Volume of water passing a point per second (m³/s). Discharge = cross-sectional area × velocity.
Input: precipitation. Stores: interception, soil, groundwater, channel. Flows: infiltration, throughflow, overland flow, percolation, groundwater flow. Outputs: evapotranspiration, discharge.
Downstream: discharge, width, depth, velocity, load volume increase; gradient, particle size, bed roughness decrease.
Time between peak rainfall and peak discharge on a storm hydrograph.
Short lag, high peak: steep slopes, impermeable rock, saturated or baked soil, little vegetation, urban areas.
Zambezi (north of the central watershed), Save and Limpopo (south and east); all reach the Indian Ocean through Mozambique.
Highest flow about April, lowest about November: rain far upstream is delayed by floodplains.
The normal flow of a river fed by groundwater between storms.
